name: Transform-based Block Coding
text:
# Transform-based Block Coding
## Overview
Transform-based block coding compresses volumetric data by partitioning it into fixed-size blocks, applying a linear transform to decorrelate values, and entropy coding the resulting coefficients [G]. It differs from global transform methods by enabling localized random access and from predictive coding by exploiting spatial frequency redundancy within blocks rather than inter-voxel differences [G]. It encompasses methods such as [ZFP Block-Based Compression](1504-zfp-block-based-compression.md), [TSDF Block Transform Coding](2548-tsdf-block-transform-coding.md), [JPEG2000](2883-jpeg2000.md), and [Learned Transform Coding](7046-learned-transform-coding.md).
## Shared principles
## Subtopics

### [ZFP Block-Based Compression](1504-zfp-block-based-compression.md)
[ZFP](#1504-zfp-block-based-compression.md) is a floating-point [compression](#4-compression.md) algorithm that encodes blocks of 4×4×4 values using fixed-rate, fixed-precision, or fixed-accuracy modes, serving as a de facto standard in the High-Performance Computing (HPC) community. It achieves up to 2 gigabytes/second throughput and excellent rate-distortion performance without introducing visual artifacts, while maintaining random access at block granularity. Unlike [learned transform coding](#7046-learned-transform-coding.md), ZFP relies on deterministic tensor-product transforms and bit-plane encoding, making it highly predictable and efficient for cache-based decompression.

### [TSDF Block Transform Coding](2548-tsdf-block-transform-coding.md)
[TSDF Block Transform Coding](#2548-tsdf-block-transform-coding.md) is a compression method for Truncated Signed Distance Function (TSDF) volumes that decomposes the input into fixed-size voxel blocks, applies a 3D [Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT)](#8014-discrete-cosine-transform-dct.md) to map spatial values to frequency coefficients, and entropy codes the retained low-frequency components. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [JPEG2000](#2883-jpeg2000.md) by using a fixed, data-independent 3D DCT kernel rather than wavelets, and from Learned Transform Coding by avoiding the need to compute and transmit scene-specific transform parameters, thereby targeting real-time [streaming](#20554-streaming.md) across arbitrary scenes.

### JPEG2000
JPEG2000 is a [wavelet-based compression](#5779-wavelet-compression-haar-basis.md) standard for still images that serves as the primary benchmark for 2-D coding systems in volumetric data compression [G]. In volume rendering, it is used as a baseline where each 2D layer of a layered image is coded separately using JPEG2000 Part-1, referred to as "Individual layer coding" [G]. This approach sets itself apart from 3D volumetric schemes by processing slices independently, which ignores inter-slice correlations and results in visible artifacts at layer boundaries compared to methods that exploit 3D redundancy [G].

### [Learned Transform Coding](7046-learned-transform-coding.md)
Learned transform coding is a compression approach used when direct rate-distortion optimization is intractable for high-dimensional data. It transforms input data $x$ into a latent representation $z$ via an encoder $E$, recovers a lossy version $\hat{x}$ from a quantized latent $\hat{z}$ via a decoder $D$, and optimizes both transformations jointly with a learned probability model for the latent. It differs from standard transform-based block coding (e.g., [JPEG2000](2883-jpeg2000.md), [ZFP Block-Based Compression](1504-zfp-block-based-compression.md)) by replacing fixed linear transforms and static entropy models with differentiable neural networks and learned priors, allowing for non-linear feature extraction and adaptive bit allocation.

### Block Transformation Coding
A technique based on block transformation coding to address difficulties of rendering large datasets on a GPU [S1].

## Background
The concept of block transformation coding for volume rendering was introduced to address the difficulties of rendering large datasets on GPUs [S1]. Fout and Ma proposed a real-time volume compression and decompression technique based on block transformation coding for use in [GPU-based raycasting](#6192-gpu-raycasting.md) pipelines [S1].
